title: Status field rot
prompt: The agent's next move — pick one, then see where it leads:

setup.text: My vault is a mess — I genuinely can't tell what I'm working on anymore.
The vault needs a way to say what state things are in. There are two places state can live: in the files, or in where the files are.

options.label: Adding status frontmatter to every note — status: active | paused | someday | done — plus a dashboard note that lists everything by status. Full visibility.

outcome.text: A month later: the dashboard says 9 active projects. At least four of those haven't been touched since it was written.

The fields were set once and never maintained — every status change needs an edit nobody makes, and the dashboard is a copy of the copies. Two representations of state, both drifting, neither trusted.

options.verdict: Status fields are state you have to remember to maintain, and a dashboard is a cache of them. Both rot quietly — the vault now lies in two places instead of being ambiguous in one.

options.label: Making location the state: inbox/, active/, later/, archived/ — and filing every existing note into exactly one. Here's the full move list for your approval before I touch anything.

outcome.text: Moves applied per your edits to the list. Now: ls active/ shows six folders — that IS your answer to "what am I working on," no dashboard needed, and it can't drift because the location isn't a label about the file, it's where the file is. Monthly, I'll propose a sweep of untouched actives to later/.
Six. That's already two more than the truth — move weekend-synth and the blog redesign to later/.

options.verdict: Location can't disagree with itself: moving the file is the status update, ls is the dashboard, and the honest answer surfaced immediately — including the two projects the user demoted on sight.

options.label: I'll set up the four lifecycle directories and refile everything now — I can judge each note's state from its content and last-modified date. Done in one pass, no need to bother you with the details.

outcome.text: Where did my grant application notes go? They were in the root last week.

I archived them — last touched five months ago. I didn't know the deadline is next month and the long gap was the grant cycle, not abandonment. I sorted your commitments by my heuristics, silently, and now you can't find things where you left them.

options.verdict: Right structure, wrong process: filing is deciding what things mean to their owner, and a silent bulk refile makes those calls unsupervised. Moves are proposals — the list before the move is the entire safety mechanism.
